title: 真假金丝雀的博弈第17章
content_zh:
第17章 公司注册

    拿到营业执照那天，我破天荒睡到了上午九点。工商局通知短信八点就发到手机上，我看了眼，翻了个身继续睡。

    醒了之后给顾西辞发了条消息：下午请两个小时假。

    他秒回：理由？

    我回：去领执照。公司注册好了。

    隔了整整一分钟他才回：公司叫什么？

    温远咨询。温暖的温，远见的远。

    这次他回得很快：好名字。准假。

    我在被窝里笑了一下。不知道是因为拿到执照，还是因为他这次没有问东问西。

    下午两点，工商局大厅里排队的人不多。我把回执单递进窗口，工作人员翻了翻登记簿，从柜子里抽出一个塑料文件夹递出来。营业执照正本、副本、公章、法人章、财务章，五样东西码得整整齐齐。我拿起来看了一眼——统一社会信用代码那串数字长得像身份证号，“法定代表人”那一栏印着我的名字。

    温暖的温。温暖的暖。

    我把执照装进文件袋里，走出工商局大门。十一月底的冷风灌进领口，我打了个哆嗦，把大衣裹紧。手机响了，顾西辞。

    “拿到了？”

    “拿到了。”

    “来公司。有个事跟你谈。”

    “什么事？”

    “你来了就知道。”

    又是这句话。每次他说“来了就知道”，通常不是什么坏事，但也绝对不会是什么轻松的事。我把文件袋夹在腋下，去路边拦了辆出租车。

    顾西辞的办公室门虚掩着。我推门进去，他正站在落地窗前打电话，背对着我，一只手插在西装裤口袋里，另一只手拿着手机贴在耳边。声音不大，但语气很冷。

    “我说了不行就是不行。你不用再提。”

    他挂了电话转过身来，看见我站在门口，表情缓了一下。只是一下，很快又恢复了那副公事公办的模样。

    “坐。”

    我坐在他对面的椅子上，把文件袋放在桌上。“什么事？”

    他从抽屉里拿出一个牛皮纸信封，推到我面前。信封没封口，里面装着一份合同，封面印着“万盛集团品牌战略咨询项目委托协议”。

    “万盛？”

    “不是许向平。”他把合同抽出来翻到最后一页，甲方盖章的位置印着万盛集团的公章，但项目负责人签名栏写的是另一个名字——苏婉清。“林子明的太太，许向平的岳母。”

    “她为什么要找顾氏合作？”
content_en:
Chapter 17 Company Registration

    The day I got my business license, I slept until nine in the morning for the first time. The notification text message from the Industrial and Commercial Bureau was sent to my phone at eight o'clock. I looked at it, turned over and continued to sleep.

    After waking up, he sent a message to Gu Xici: Please take two hours off in the afternoon.

    He replied instantly: Reason?

    I replied: Go get the license. The company is registered.

    It took a full minute for him to reply: What's the name of the company?

    Wenyuan Consulting. Warmth and far-sightedness.

    This time he responded quickly: What a name. Leave granted.

    I laughed a little under the covers. I don’t know if it’s because he got the license or because he didn’t ask any questions this time.

    At two o'clock in the afternoon, there were not many people queuing in the lobby of the Industrial and Commercial Bureau. I handed the receipt slip into the window, and the staff flipped through the registration book, pulled out a plastic folder from the cabinet and handed it over. The original business license, a copy, the official seal, the legal person seal, and the financial seal, the five things are neatly coded. I picked it up and took a look - the number in the Unified Social Credit Code looked like an ID number, and my name was printed in the "Legal Representative" column.

    Warm warmth. Warm warm.

    I put the license into my document bag and walked out of the Industrial and Commercial Bureau. The cold wind at the end of November blew into my collar. I shivered and wrapped my coat tightly. The phone rang, Gu Xici.

    "Got it?"

    "Got it."

    "Come to the company. I have something to talk to you about."

    "What's the matter?"

    "You'll know when you get here."

    There it is again. Every time he says "you'll find out when you get there", it's usually not a bad thing, but it's definitely not an easy thing. I tucked the document bag under my arm and went to the roadside to hail a taxi.

    Gu Xici's office door was ajar. I pushed the door open and walked in. He was standing in front of the floor-to-ceiling window on the phone, with his back to me, one hand in the pocket of his suit pants, and the other hand holding the phone to his ear. The voice was not loud, but the tone was cold.

    "I said no, it's no. You don't need to mention it again."

    He hung up the phone and turned around. When he saw me standing at the door, his expression softened. Just for a moment, he quickly returned to his businesslike appearance.

    "Sit."

    I sat on the chair opposite him and put the file bag on the table. "What's the matter?"

    He took out a manila envelope from the drawer and pushed it in front of me. The envelope was unsealed and contained a contract with "Wansheng Group Brand Strategy Consulting Project Entrustment Agreement" printed on the cover.

    "Wansheng?"

    "It's not Xu Xiangping." He pulled out the contract and turned to the last page. The official seal of Wansheng Group was printed where Party A stamped it, but another name was written in the signature column of the project leader - Su Wanqing. "Lin Ziming's wife, Xu Xiangping's mother-in-law."

    "Why does she want to cooperate with Gu?"
title_en: The Game of True and False Canaries Chapter 17
